headline: 4 crude bombs explode as Awami League activists march in Dhanmondi
summary: Police dispersed a brief procession of the banned party's leaders and activists on Saturday, detaining three people.
details: Leaders and activists of the Awami League, whose activities have been banned, staged a brief procession in Dhaka’s Dhanmondi area on Saturday.
The procession, which took place around 12:15 pm on Road No. 27, involved participants chanting ‘Joy Bangla’.
According to Dhanmondi Police Station chief Muhammad Imdadul Islam, police dispersed the group and reported four crude bomb explosions during the incident.
Witnesses stated the march began near Ibn Sina Hospital and continued toward the Bata outlet on Road 27 before police gave chase.
Police have detained three individuals and are currently checking their identities and backgrounds before taking legal action.
This incident follows a similar attempt by Awami League members and affiliated organisations in Gulshan on September 11, where police used rubber bullets to disperse the crowd.
In the case filed over the Gulshan incident, police say 179 people have already been arrested.
The Gulshan event prompted changes in the local police leadership due to widespread discussion of the incident.

headline_marked: 4 arrested after [[health center demolished]] in Mirpur
headline: 4 arrested after health center demolished in Mirpur
summary: Police arrested four suspects in connection with the midnight raid on the Radda MCH-FP Center, where over 200 masked men destroyed the facility.
details: Police have arrested four individuals in connection with the midnight demolition and looting of the Radda MCH-FP Center in Mirpur-1, Dhaka.
The suspects, aged 20 to 23, were arrested during a raid on Friday night. According to Shah Ali Police Station, the arrested men have confessed to their involvement in the attack.
Investigations reveal that three of the suspects are homeless individuals from the Shah Ali Mazar area who were allegedly paid to participate in the demolition.

The attack occurred around midnight last Thursday. Over 200 masked men armed with indigenous weapons entered the center, took two security guards hostage, and looted valuable equipment, medicines, and vaccines.
The attackers then used heavy machinery to demolish one permanent building and three semi-permanent buildings within the facility.
The Radda MCH-FP Center, established in 1974, provides essential maternal and child health services, including vaccinations and reproductive health care for low-income families in Mirpur.
The center's executive director, Nasrin Akhtar, confirmed that a case has been filed at Shah Ali Police Station, and the investigation is ongoing.
